clue.text: Lively liturgy has brought about rise in baptisms

indicators.note: to bring something about here is to wrap around it, so one word ends up enclosing the other
in a down clue a rise reads the word from the bottom up, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: baptism by immersion is a dip in the water
a liturgy is a set form of religious rite

explanation.surface: A church service livened up by a rise in the number of christenings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lively liturgy' reads as one phrase, but only 'Lively' defines; dipping is the immersion part of a baptism.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirited and lively are synonyms, both describing energetic, animated behaviour full of vigour.

clue.text: Confused, having thrown up Toy Story V, nothing less

indicators.note: letters that have been thrown about land in a jumbled new order
less means minus, so the following letter is taken away from the fodder

parts.note: taken as written
the film title with its Roman numeral, taken as written
nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone baffled after hurling a fifth Toy Story film skywards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown up' reads as one phrase, but 'up' is part of the fodder; drop one O from UP + TOYSTORYV and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Topsy-turvy describes things upside down or in utter disorder, a muddled state like being confused.

clue.text: State University leading cover up

indicators.note: leading means coming in front, so this piece starts the entry

parts.note: standard abbreviation for university

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending a word up reads its letters from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a hat is a head covering

explanation.surface: A state university heading a cover-up scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty states of the USA, so it is an example of a state.

clue.text: Duke is first to Haydock course

parts.note: standard abbreviation for duke
taken as written

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: opening letter of the place name

explanation.surface: A duke is the first to arrive at Haydock racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Haydock Park is an English horse-racing course, so 'course' looks like a racecourse; it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is one part of a meal served at once, the same thing as a course such as starter or dessert.

clue.text: First nine letters of alphabet written up — culminating in this?

definitions.text: First nine letters of alphabet written up — culminating in this?

indicators.note: in a down clue, writing a phrase upwards puts its letters in reverse order

parts.note: the first nine letters run from A to I

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where the first nine letters of an alphabet end up.
explanation.walkthrough: A TO I reads upwards as IOTA, and in the Greek alphabet the ninth letter is iota, so the first nine Greek letters culminate in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet, the last of its first nine characters.

clue.text: Indignation, after river blocked — no power now?

indicators.note: something blocked is shut out, so this letter is kept out of the word

parts.note: outrage is strong indignation
standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Anger when the river is dammed and the electricity fails.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R out of OUTRAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An outage is a period when the electricity supply is cut, leaving a home without electric current.

clue.text: Talk a lot about Republican growth

indicators.note: about means around, so one word is placed surrounding the other letter

parts.note: to spout is to talk at length
standard abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Someone holding forth at length about a Republican economic boom.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprout is a new shoot on a plant, a piece of fresh growth.

clue.text: Last item recalled European Union attempt to mislead about power

indicators.note: called back, so the whole string is read in the opposite direction
about means surrounding, so the word for misleading goes around the next letter

parts.note: the usual abbreviation
to have a go is to make an attempt
to lie is to mislead
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A final agenda item recalling an EU bid to mislead people about energy.
explanation.walkthrough: EU + GO + LI(P)E makes EUGOLIPE, which read backwards gives EPILOGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epilogue is the closing section of a book or play, the final piece that comes after everything else.

clue.text: Each solicitor will have to go for a meal

parts.note: standard abbreviation for each
a tout solicits custom, so is one who solicits

explanation.surface: Every lawyer must head off to lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a lawyer, but here it is someone who solicits business: a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat out is to have a meal at a restaurant rather than home, the same as going for a meal.

clue.text: Angry getting access to lower deck in shade

parts.note: cross means annoyed
a hatch is an opening in a ship's deck leading below

explanation.surface: A sailor furious at reaching the lower deck while lurking in the shadows.
explanation.definitionFit: To crosshatch is to shade a drawing with intersecting sets of parallel lines.

clue.text: A good outcome for those visiting on holiday?

definitions.text: A good outcome for those visiting
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a win by the visiting team in sport
second meaning: not at home, off on a trip

explanation.walkthrough: Visitors sounds like tourists, but in football the visiting side plays an away game, and an away win is a good result for them.
explanation.definitionFit: An away result favours visiting teams in sport, and someone away is absent from home, as on holiday.

clue.text: Satisfy audience about tense gathering of legislators

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the first word wraps the next letter

parts.note: to sate is to satisfy fully
grammatical abbreviation for tense
the house is the audience in a theatre

explanation.surface: Pleasing a crowd at a fraught political meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: S(T)ATE, then HOUSE. A statehouse is the American name for a state's legislative building.
explanation.definitionFit: A statehouse is where a US state's lawmakers meet, standing by metonymy for the legislature assembled there.

clue.text: Underworld keeps around half of dead

indicators.note: something kept around is held inside, so the first word encloses the next piece

parts.note: to have is to keep or hold

indicators.note: only one of the two halves of the following word is used

parts.note: first half of the four-letter word

explanation.surface: The realm of the dead holding on to some of its departed.
explanation.walkthrough: HA(DE)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Hades is the Greek underworld, realm of departed souls ruled by the god of the same name.

clue.text: Anesthetic, article found in part of US hospital

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so the article sits within the hospital department

parts.note: the emergency room, the American casualty department
the definite article

explanation.surface: An item about anaesthetics discovered in an American emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: E(THE)R.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was one of the first general anaesthetics, inhaled to put surgical patients to sleep.

clue.text: Game? Put off, losing heart

indicators.note: a word that loses its heart drops its central letter

parts.note: to deter is to put off

explanation.surface: Someone asked if they fancy a game but discouraged and losing their nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like an offer to play; it means animals hunted for food. Remove the middle T from DETER.
explanation.definitionFit: Game is wild animals hunted for sport or meat, and deer are a classic example of such quarry.

clue.text: Walking through feathers, perhaps rather shabby

parts.note: down is soft fine feathering, an example of feathers
a dog walking obediently by its owner's leg is at heel

explanation.surface: Someone wading through a heap of plumage looking a bit scruffy.
explanation.definitionFit: Down-at-heel describes someone poorly dressed and run-down, with worn shoes, so looking shabby.

clue.text: Fear shifting article forward? Took the risk

indicators.note: the moved letter is put back in further forward, nearer the start of the word
shifting a letter takes it out of its current position before it is placed elsewhere

parts.note: dread is great fear
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A nervous writer moving a piece up the page and taking a chance.
explanation.walkthrough: In DREAD the A moves one place towards the front: D-A-RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Dared is the past tense of dare, meaning ventured to do something bold despite the danger.

clue.text: Short vacation — about week? Sounds of protest

indicators.note: about means around, so the holiday word surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: hols is British shorthand for holidays
standard abbreviation for week

explanation.surface: Complaints when a break lasts only about a week.
explanation.walkthrough: HO(W)LS; 'short' shortens holidays to the British colloquial hols.
explanation.definitionFit: Howls are loud cries, often of complaint, as in howls of protest from an angry public.

clue.text: Controller is upset about mercenary seizing Government

indicators.note: about means around, so the overturned word encloses what follows
something upset is turned over, so in a down clue its letters run upwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the mercenary word grips the next letter

parts.note: venal means open to bribery, mercenary
standard abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: A ruler is dismayed about a hired soldier taking over the state.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: the government letter goes inside the mercenary word first. Svengali is the hypnotist in George du Maurier's novel Trilby.
explanation.definitionFit: A Svengali is someone who manipulates and dominates another person, a sinister puppet-master figure.

clue.text: Actors: pair late on in Hamlet, in Elsinore?

definitions.note: the question mark marks this as an example: Elsinore is the castle setting of Hamlet

indicators.note: only a couple of letters lying towards the end of the next word are kept, the rest discarded

parts.note: the cast is the company of actors in a production
the play's title, taken as written

explanation.surface: The players in Hamlet, a couple of them entering late in the action, at Elsinore.
explanation.walkthrough: Elsinore is Shakespeare's name for Kronborg, the Danish royal castle where Hamlet is set.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsinore is a castle, the fortress at Helsingør, so the place stands as an example of the answer.

clue.text: The writer backed the writer's award

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the pronoun is read in reverse

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter, so me
belonging to the setter, so my

explanation.surface: An author supported the prize-winning writer.
explanation.definitionFit: An Emmy is the American television industry's annual award, a statuette for excellence in TV.

clue.text: Married, affectionate, though not initially poignant

indicators.note: not initially means without its opening letter, so the first one is dropped

parts.note: standard abbreviation for married
loving means affectionate

explanation.surface: A wedded couple, fond but not at first, in a touching story.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moving stirs deep emotion, especially sadness or sympathy, just as a poignant scene does.

clue.text: Problems for disabled access? Assist disabled with care

indicators.note: something disabled is broken, so these letters are put back in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Helping people with disabilities into a building, with sensitivity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disabled' appears twice: the first is part of the definition, the second the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Flights of steps are barriers to wheelchair users, so they are typical obstacles to accessible buildings.

clue.text: Completed insurance, shelling out $100

indicators.note: shelling out here means removing a shell, so this letter is stripped away

parts.note: insurance provides cover
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A policy taken out, with a hundred dollars paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelling out' suggests paying; it means taking C out of COVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Over means finished or ended, as when a match is over and its play is complete.

clue.text: First person in Germany to support King with money

indicators.note: in a down entry a support goes underneath, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: R for rex, Latin for king
ich is German for I, the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: A German leader being first to back the king financially.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich means wealthy, having plenty of cash and possessions.

clue.text: Not your usual breakfast item — startled grocer reduced this — good

indicators.note: startled letters jump about and land in a different order
reduced means cut short, so the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A grocer alarmed at being handed an unusual breakfast to sell.
explanation.walkthrough: Shorten GROCER to GROCE, add THIS and rearrange, then add G.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostrich egg is edible but enormous, roughly two dozen hens' eggs, so hardly a normal morning meal.

clue.text: Old science magazine occupying fandom nightly

indicators.note: the answer occupies space inside the next words, sitting within them

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A defunct science magazine engrossing its fans every night.
explanation.definitionFit: Omni was an American science and science-fiction magazine published from 1978 to 1995.

clue.text: Lot of information on computer about a foot

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first
about means turned round, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: AI, artificial intelligence, stands for a computer brain
a megabyte is a large quantity of data

explanation.surface: A large data file on a computer about the size of a foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A foot' looks like a length of twelve inches; here a foot is a metrical unit in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical foot of one unstressed syllable followed by a stressed one.

clue.text: Position computer key formerly around third in line

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the key name goes around the selected letter

parts.note: the Escape key

indicators.note: third in points to the letter in third place of the next word

parts.note: third letter of the word
once means at a former time

explanation.surface: Placing the computer key that was once next to the line.
explanation.walkthrough: E(N)SC, then ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensconce is to settle or establish oneself firmly in a place, so to position.

clue.text: Part of intestine repelled, having received small breakfast?

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the word runs backwards
a word that has received something holds it inside

parts.note: the ileum is the last section of the small intestine
standard abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A bowel complaint after a light morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: ILEUM reversed is MUELI, which takes in S: MUE(S)LI.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a cereal mix of oats, nuts and dried fruit eaten in the morning; the question mark shows an example.
